text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2025 E 350 rates the build quality as excellent. Owner states the four-cylinder E 350 has sufficient power and runs at only about 1,300 rpm at 65 mph. Owner states the cabin is quiet at highway speed. Owner reports about 42 mpg on the highway with two people aboard and cruise control set at 65 mph. Owner states the air vents give very good airflow without blowing directly on the occupants. Owner finds the voice command system helpful. Owner states the voice assistant sometimes activates unexpectedly. Owner states rear foot room is too tight, making a one-hour trip in the back uncomfortable; a 2024 Toyota Camry's rear seat felt more comfortable. Owner finds getting in and out of the car difficult, even after adjusting the seat. Owner misses a front seat thigh extension for tall drivers and passengers. Owner reports the adaptive cruise control braked hard without warning on the highway, dropping from 65 to 35 mph, most often near exits. Owner states lane departure warning gives only a faint steering-wheel vibration and does not steer the car back, unlike the family's Toyota, Hyundai and VW cars. Owner complains there is no spare tire; with run-flat tires, a flat after hours or on a weekend meant waiting about two days for a replacement. Owner states the touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls change the instrument cluster display too easily. Owner reports the right windshield wiper makes a loud noise in light rain, and a friend's car has the same issue. Owner finds the standard speakers adequate, although louder audio would need the roughly $1,000 Burmester 4D option. Owner questions spending about $72,000 on the car and says they would not make the same purchase again.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2021 G80 3.5T AWD Prestige states the car is a pleasure to drive. Owner praises the value of the car. Owner states the dealerships sell a luxury car in a not-so-luxurious environment. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «a pleasure to drive»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a first-year new-design G80 criticizes the four-cylinder engine and its vibration. Owner states fuel economy is worse than with the previous model's 3.8-liter engine. Owner criticizes cheap plastic parts and poor build quality. Owner states the automatic emergency braking does not work. Owner states the lane control behaves erratically. Owner reports dealer service problems, states the manufacturer refused repairs and mentions the lemon law. Owner states the G80 looks great while calling the rest of the car a step backwards.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the driver-attention 'consider taking a break' alert fires randomly every 5 to 30 minutes with a loud beep and cannot be turned off; they call it a deal breaker.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a G80 2.5 Prestige RWD, previously a Lexus ES owner, praises the power. Owner praises the smooth ride. Owner praises how quiet the car is. Owner states the car stays comfortable on 9-hour drives and praises the massaging seats. Owner praises the interior. Owner praises the sound system.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2024 G80 3.5T Sport Prestige (their third G80) praises the ride, handling and braking. Owner praises the acceleration. Owner praises the interior. Owner praises the 21-speaker sound system. Owner praises the value of the car. Owner states the 2024 model dropped the rear window shades and soft-close doors of the 2021 and would give up the rear-wheel steering to get them back.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the car's attractive looks. Owner dislikes the two-spoke steering wheel. Owner wants a fully digital gauge cluster included with the Advanced package.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the gas mileage. Owner praises the ride and handling. Owner praises the styling. Owner notes a brief delay when accelerating hard.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a new 2022 G80 complains that the car has no wireless phone charging pad.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner, who previously owned a BMW 5 Series (earlier generation, not G60), states the G80's back seat is spacious unlike the 5 Series'. Owner praises the smooth ride and handling. Owner praises the styling. Owner reports no mechanical issues in the first three months. Owner praises the value of the car. Owner wants Genesis to develop its own dealer network. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «Genesis needs to develop its own dealer network»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2021 ES 300h hybrid praises the safety features. Owner reports a consistent 43-44 mpg from the hybrid. Owner finds the large screen easy to read and says the touchpad is easy to get used to, dismissing negative touchpad reviews. Owner finds the seats firmer than they would like.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2020 ES 350 reports excessive wind and road noise, especially a rushing noise from the rear side window, that the dealer failed to fix in two attempts. Owner states the dealer said acoustic windows would help but they are only fitted to the Luxury trim, which was not disclosed in writing.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the strong engine response of the V6. Senior owner calls the car easy to drive and reliable, the best and last car they will own.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner reports five years of ownership with no problems. Owner praises the smooth, relaxing ride on short and long trips.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2019 ES 350 tells shoppers looking at the 5-Series (also E-Class, G80) that the ES is the best choice, citing price and reliability. Owner praises the luxury features such as heated and cooled seats, moonroof and power trunk lid at an affordable price. Owner praises the plush ride. Owner praises the passing power. Owner concedes the ES is less performance-oriented than its European competitors.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2024 ES F Sport praises the safety technology. Owner praises the quiet ride. Owner praises the F Sport styling.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2024 ES 250 AWD Luxury praises the build quality and materials. Owner values all-wheel drive for snow, noting the ES 350 is not offered with AWD. Owner praises the quiet cabin and highway comfort. Owner wants heated or ventilated rear seats and rear climate controls, which the car lacks. Owner regrets the removal of the CD player. Owner states the infotainment system needs updating. Owner reports problems with the wireless phone charger. Owner states the front parking sensors beep constantly when covered with snow. Owner finds the fuel economy of about 22-26 mpg modest for a four-cylinder. Owner dislikes having to pay extra for the better stereo.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2025 ES 300h praises the comfort and serenity on the highway. Owner praises the smooth hybrid drivetrain. Owner praises the fuel economy and low running costs. Owner notes the rear seats do not fold down.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a CT5 Premium Luxury 2.0T (bought Aug 2022) praises the comfortable seats. Owner praises the rear legroom. Owner likes the fold-down rear seats. Owner likes the wood and leather trim. Owner praises the engine power. Owner praises the fuel economy. Owner praises the sound system. Owner reports no issues in the first nine months and likes the dealer's pickup and return service. Owner notes the trunk is smaller (than their previous CTS). Owner finds the suspension soft and wishes it had more adjustment. Owner wants massage seats, which are not offered with the four-cylinder. Owner wanted a paint color and the Sedona leather that could not be ordered for their configuration.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an AWD CT5 Luxury with 21,000 miles reports up to 36 mpg. Owner finds the car has more power than expected. Owner praises the nice ride and good handling.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2020 CT5 Sport 2.0T praises the engine power and the performance shift mode. Owner likes the lumbar massage, extendable seat cushion and driver footrest. Owner likes the Bose audio system. Owner likes the snow mode with AWD and the handling in sport mode. Owner praises the reliability.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a CT5-V with the Platinum package praises the engine performance. Owner praises the engine sound. Owner praises the luxury of the Platinum package.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a CT5 Premium Luxury V6 finds visibility poor, solved by adding the camera package. Owner's car has no sunroof and they list that as a dislike. Owner praises the V6 performance. Owner likes the Bose sound system. Owner likes the styling.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the ride and driving feel. Owner praises the premium components.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a CT5 Premium Luxury 3.0 V6 praises the power. Owner praises the ride and handling in traffic. Owner praises the 15-speaker Bose system.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a CT5 Sport states it outperforms the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes C-Class they also shopped (3 Series, not 5 Series). Owner finds the car roomy for a family of four, with enough trunk space. Owner praises the premium leather and carbon details. Owner praises the smooth, sporty and comfortable ride. Owner praises the premium audio. Owner likes the looks inside and out. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «outperforms the BMW 3 series and Mercedes C class»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a Model S Plaid with the yoke praises the acceleration. Owner likes the yoke steering. Owner likes the expansive display. Owner praises the cabin space. Owner values the hatchback. Owner likes the adjustable air suspension. Owner criticizes the brakes and wants the Track Pack brakes to be standard. Owner complains that negative camber, which cannot be adjusted, wears the tires. Owner complains about cabin noise. Owner notes power is limited in winter.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a Model S Plaid bought new in 2021 praises the speed. Owner praises the comfort. Owner praises the self-driving features. Owner values Supercharger access. Owner reports rapid wear on the inner edges of the rear tires.
